tagline: Up the Bear River and through the notch to Umbagog.
intro: Route 26 leaves Newry just north of the Sunday River ski area and follows the Bear River up into Grafton Notch, the pass between Baldpate and Old Speck, the fourth-highest mountain in Maine. Over the notch it comes down to Upton, a town of 69 people at the 2020 census, and Lake Umbagog on the New Hampshire line.

Old farmhouses and weathered stone walls mark the valley, and much of the land is state park or working forest now. The notch is glacier work, a U-shaped valley with boulders the ice left scattered across its floor.

moments.title: Screw Auger Falls
moments.text: The Bear River drops through a steep gorge cut in Devonian granite, and when the water runs low the boulders the glacier left show in the stream.

moments.title: Umbagog Lake
moments.text: The name is said to be Abenaki for shallow water, and off the northwest shore floats an island made of generations of decaying marsh plants.
